editorial:
Imagine having a father who is the most popular guy in Hollywood, but he is the one person you cannot get along with. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow Abbie, a stressed-out New York doctor who has a heart attack and heads to LA to reconnect with his dad, Abe. Abe is the king of background actors, meaning he spends his life being an extra in movies. He is full of life and loves everyone, but his relationship with his son is cold and distant. It is a sweet, bittersweet setup that feels like a warm hug, blending some funny Hollywood moments with a very real family struggle.

You will really feel for these characters as Abe starts losing his memory due to a brain aneurysm. The acting is top-notch, and the way the father and son slowly fix their bond is genuinely touching. While the pace is a bit slower than a modern blockbuster, it gives you time to actually care about the people on screen. If you are in the mood for a real tear-jerker, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: As Abe's health gets worse, Abbie stops focusing on his own anger and does everything he can to make his father happy. He manages to land Abe a real speaking role in a movie, giving him the spotlight he always wanted. They finally make peace and share a deep, loving bond before Abe passes away. It ends on a sad but beautiful note, showing that it is never too late to say I love you.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and stories about second chances.
